rows.label: V1 production
rows.quitText: If you've got SMU or Louisville or Clemson, vote in the Pulse below and bring the football with you: a name, a date, and the game where they take this league away. Check the Ledger any Saturday to see how this one is holding up. That's all I've been asking since the question came in.
smell: Every preseason produces one take so popular that people start distrusting it for no reason beyond the size of the crowd standing on it.
Best team in the ACC and winner of the ACC are two separate bets, and the popular take sells you the second one at the price of the first.
This is an argument by elimination, which is the cheapest way to win one.

It gives one other program in this conference a head-to-head result over Miami, which is the only currency that converts a coronation into a race, and it makes every Miami Saturday after it read differently.

So take the unhedged version. Miami is the best team in this conference by a distance, the other sixteen are playing for second, and Clemson on October 3 is the single result that pulls me back to the table.

rows.label: V2 (loop 4)
rows.quitText: The Clemson objection is the easy one to state: my own board has them ahead of the team I keep calling the runaway ACC favorite, so why exactly am I waving them off as an alternative? Fair. I don't have a tidy answer beyond the fact that a national ranking and a conference favorite tag are answering slightly different questions, and that Clemson's finished 2025 record is the only thing either of us can actually point to.
smell: That is the first date on Miami's schedule where a broad opinion about the ACC has to become a result, and it happens to involve one of the three teams I named out loud as the only realistic alternatives to Miami.
Where I'd push is on why the contradiction makes the game more interesting rather than less.
Which is why I'd separate October 3 from the game everyone will circle instead.
A Clemson win hands my rhetorical question a specific, immediate answer, and I'd have to say so plainly.
What it will do is put a scoreboard behind two of my numbers that currently disagree with each other.

rows.label: D · Josh's hand edit
smell: That is a twelve-spot gap inside one league, and it is the widest gap between a conference's first and second teams anywhere in the preseason polls.
And understand what October 3 actually decides, because it is more than one line in the loss column.
If the Mustangs turn in both, the "then who" question gets a real answer, and I'll write that column too.
By the first weekend of October we will know whether this was a race or a coronation.
So I'm planting it. Miami is the overwhelming ACC favorite, and Clemson on October 3 is the one result that makes me reopen the race.
